genZNote: Won't even show up on a regular Gram stain and refuses to grow unless you feed it cysteine and iron — high maintenance, high mortality.

morphology.notes: Stains poorly with standard Gram stain (faintly Gram-negative); often better visualized with Dieterle silver stain or direct fluorescent antibody testing

habitat.naturalHabitat: Freshwater environments — lakes, streams, and especially man-made water systems
habitat.hostAssociation: Facultative intracellular pathogen of free-living amoebae in nature; infects human alveolar macrophages after inhalation
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Thrives in biofilms within cooling towers, plumbing systems, hot tubs, and decorative fountains, especially warm, stagnant water
habitat.reservoir: Man-made water systems (cooling towers, potable water plumbing, hot tubs)

microscopy.stain: Dieterle silver stain or direct fluorescent antibody (DFA); poorly visualized on standard Gram stain

culture.media: Buffered charcoal yeast extract (BCYE) agar with L-cysteine and iron — will not grow on standard blood/MacConkey agar
culture.growthCharacteristics: Obligate aerobe; slow-growing, requires 3-5 days incubation
culture.colonyMorphology: Gray-white, ground-glass colonies with a distinctive 'cut-glass' iridescent sheen under oblique light
culture.hemolysis: Not applicable — not routinely tested on blood agar

identificationClues: Faintly Gram-negative rod that stains poorly on routine Gram stain
Will only grow on BCYE agar supplemented with L-cysteine and iron — no growth on standard media
Urinary antigen test detects Legionella serogroup 1 (the most common cause of disease) rapidly and non-invasively
Linked to contaminated water systems — cooling towers, plumbing, hot tubs — with no person-to-person spread

diseases: Legionnaires' disease — severe pneumonia, often with GI symptoms (diarrhea), confusion, hyponatremia, and relative bradycardia
Pontiac fever — a milder, self-limited flu-like illness without pneumonia
virulenceFactors: Facultative intracellular survival and replication within alveolar macrophages (evades phagosome-lysosome fusion)
Type IV secretion system (Dot/Icm) injecting effector proteins into host cells
clinicalImportance.transmission: Inhalation of aerosolized water droplets from contaminated sources (cooling towers, showers, hot tubs); no person-to-person transmission
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: A significant cause of both community-acquired and healthcare-associated pneumonia, with outbreaks traced to contaminated building water systems; disproportionately affects smokers, the elderly, and immunocompromised patients
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: Routine sputum Gram stain and culture will miss Legionella entirely — diagnosis requires urinary antigen testing, specific BCYE culture, or PCR when Legionella is clinically suspected

examFacts.keyBiochemicalReaction: Requires L-cysteine and iron; grows only on BCYE agar
examFacts.importantTest: Urinary antigen test (serogroup 1); culture on BCYE agar
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: An intracellular pathogen of water-system biofilms and amoebae that requires special BCYE culture media and doesn't spread person-to-person
